sentences.text: CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RATNAKER BHENGRA -------

For the Petitioner : Mr. Kaushik Sarkhel, Advocate  : Mr. Rishu Ranjan, Advocate  : Mr. Abhishek Singh, Advocate  For the State : Mr. Saket Kumar, APP  --------
05 /16.02.2024  Heard the learned counsels for the parties.
The petitioner is an accused in a case registered under sections 376 & 313 of the Indian Penal Code and sections 4 & 8 of POCSO Act.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the allegations have been made by the victim who was already married on 19.05.2021 with another person.
It is further submitted that prior to this date of marriage also there is allegations that in the year 2019 on 15.07.2019 petitioner had established sexual relationship.
It is further submitted that second date of occurrence is allegedly on 20.04.2023 when she was already married with another person.

It is further stated that the FIR was also delayed and the FIR was lodged on 01.05.2023 which has been delayed by about 10 to 11 days at least from the alleged second occurrence, so on this basis there is suspicion regarding the allegations.

It is further submitted that in her medical examination doctor has said that she was 12 weeks pregnant which would mean that she was already pregnant from before because she was in a married relationship and thus no where it has come that the pregnancy is the result of union with this petitioner.

The learned counsel has further submitted that even in the year 2019 she has lodged an occurrence thereafter she had got married and in the year 2023 she still wanted to continue with the relationship and had come to the petitioner on her own volition and it is only because the petitioner was not inclined to continue the relationship she had lodged the case and when apparently villagers had come to know about the relationship realizing that many other persons had Govind Kumar @ Gobind Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ... 1 come to know then she has lodged the case.

sentences.text: Moreover in the circumstances, the petitioner is in custody from 24.05.2023 and therefore based on the aforesaid circumstances, the custody is also punitive and therefore, the petitioner may be allowed the privilege of bail.

Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the bail petition and submitted that the victim is a minor, her date of birth according to Aadhar Card is 17.10.2006 and therefore on the date of second occurrence she would be around 17 years and therefore below 18 years and therefore she would be a minor, if the first date of occurrence of the year 2019 is taken into consideration then she would definitely be below 16 years.

It is further submitted that many persons have supported the prosecution case and in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. the victim has also supported the prosecution case, therefore, the petitioner may not be allowed the privilege of bail.

Having heard both counsels, gone through the records of the case, noted the submissions and in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to release the petitioner, named above, on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge 1, Ramgarh in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 21 of 2023 arising out of Rajrappa P.S. Case No. 67 of 2023 , subject to the condition that the petitioner shall remain present on each and every date of trial before the Court below unless dispensed with by the learned Court below with further condition that the petitioner will submit self-attested photocopy of his Aadhaar Card and also submit his mobile number before the learned court below which he will always keep active and will not change it during pendency of this case without prior permission of the court.

(Ratnaker Bhengra, J.) Sharda/
